notes: ostag/briefs/models.py:_timezone_keys — exact-key enforcement is correct: membership in frozenset(zoneinfo.available_timezones()) is case-sensitive regardless of filesystem, so 'utc'/'america/los_angeles' are rejected on macOS while real registry aliases (US/Pacific, Etc/UTC) remain accepted because available_timezones() enumerates backward-compat link files and the tzdata zones list.

Error translation is scoped correctly: only OSError is caught in the registry path and only (ValueError, ZoneInfoNotFoundError, OSError) in the loader path; TypeError/RuntimeError propagate. lru_cache does not memoize raised exceptions, so a failed scan is not cached (verified by test_timezone_registry_io_failure_does_not_cache_a_failed_scan, scans == 2).

Tests are meaningful, not rubber stamps: the permissive case-insensitive fake loader would make the old ZoneInfo-only validator accept 'utc'/'US/pacific', so test_timezone_rejects_non_registry_keys_with_permissive_loader fails against the previous implementation and passes only with registry membership. Monkeypatch targets are correct (zoneinfo.available_timezones is called via module attribute; models.ZoneInfo is the imported name). Fixture clears the lru_cache at setup and teardown so cached real-registry state cannot leak into faked tests or vice versa.

Ordering in TimeWindow.__post_init__ (UTC parsing, ordering check, _text, registry membership, loader, then normalization) leaves timestamp, grant, source, audience and immutability semantics unchanged; _window still revalidates via replace().

Non-blocking observation: CPython's available_timezones() internally swallows most per-file I/O errors and returns an empty set when no tzdata is present, so in that environment every display_timezone becomes a SchemaError (and the empty registry is cached). This is consistent with the contract (invalid zone) but operators may want a startup check that the registry is non-empty in a future server-wiring task.

Non-blocking: registry keys such as 'localtime' or 'posixrules' variants that some distros ship as TZif files would be admitted if present; ZoneInfo accepts them too, so this matches prior behavior and is not a regression.
